questions.question: What is the rate-determining step in the electrophilic aromatic substitution (EAS) bromination of benzene?

options.label: A
options.text: Attack of the aromatic π system on the electrophilic Br⁺ equivalent (Br₂·FeBr₃) to form the non-aromatic resonance-stabilized arenium ion (sigma complex).

options.label: B
options.text: Coordination of FeBr₃ with benzene.

options.label: C
options.text: Deprotonation of the arenium ion by FeBr₄⁻.

options.label: D
options.text: Dissociation of bromobenzene into ions.

questions.correct_answer: Attack of the aromatic π system on the electrophilic Br⁺ equivalent (Br₂·FeBr₃) to form the non-aromatic resonance-stabilized arenium ion (sigma complex).
questions.explanation: Formation of the sigma complex disrupts aromaticity, making it the slow, rate-determining endothermic step.

questions.question: Why is the second step (deprotonation of the arenium ion) in EAS extraordinarily fast and exergonic?

options.label: A
options.text: The arenium ion is an explosive intermediate.

options.label: B
options.text: Loss of a proton from the sp³ carbon rehybridizes it to sp², instantly restoring the massive 150 kJ/mol aromatic resonance stabilization energy of the benzene ring.

options.label: C
options.text: The base FeBr₄⁻ is a superacid.

options.label: D
options.text: The reaction releases elemental bromine gas.

questions.correct_answer: Loss of a proton from the sp³ carbon rehybridizes it to sp², instantly restoring the massive 150 kJ/mol aromatic resonance stabilization energy of the benzene ring.
questions.explanation: Regaining aromaticity provides a powerful thermodynamic driving force that makes deprotonation extremely rapid.

questions.question: How is the active electrophile (NO₂⁺) generated in the nitration of benzene by HNO₃ / H₂SO₄?

options.label: A
options.text: Sulfuric acid oxidizes nitrogen dioxide to nitrate.

options.label: B
options.text: Sulfuric acid protonates the hydroxyl oxygen of nitric acid to form H₂O⁺-NO₂, which spontaneously loses water to generate the linear nitronium cation (O=N⁺=O).

options.label: C
options.text: Nitric acid directly attacks benzene without acid catalysis.

options.label: D
options.text: Nitric acid undergoes homolytic cleavage to NO₂ radicals.

questions.correct_answer: Sulfuric acid protonates the hydroxyl oxygen of nitric acid to form H₂O⁺-NO₂, which spontaneously loses water to generate the linear nitronium cation (O=N⁺=O).
questions.explanation: Protonation of nitric acid turns -OH into water, a good leaving group, expelling H₂O to liberate the powerful nitronium electrophile.

questions.question: Why do Friedel-Crafts acylations avoid carbocation rearrangements whereas Friedel-Crafts alkylations frequently rearrange?

options.label: A
options.text: Acyl halides generate resonance-stabilized acylium ions [R-C⁺=O ↔ R-C≡O⁺] where all atoms satisfy the octet rule, preventing 1,2-hydride or alkyl shifts.

options.label: B
options.text: Acylation proceeds via an SN2 mechanism on the ring.

options.label: C
options.text: Aluminum chloride destroys all carbocations.

options.label: D
options.text: Acylium ions are too small to undergo rearrangements.

questions.correct_answer: Acyl halides generate resonance-stabilized acylium ions [R-C⁺=O ↔ R-C≡O⁺] where all atoms satisfy the octet rule, preventing 1,2-hydride or alkyl shifts.
questions.explanation: The acylium ion is resonance-stabilized with an octet-complete [R-C≡O⁺] major contributor, making it immune to skeletal rearrangements.

questions.question: Why does a methoxy group (-OCH₃) direct incoming electrophiles predominantly to the ortho and para positions?

options.label: A
options.text: The methoxy group sterically blocks the meta positions.

options.label: B
options.text: Lone pair donation from oxygen provides an additional, fourth resonance contributor for ortho and para sigma complexes where every atom has a full octet.

options.label: C
options.text: The methoxy group is strongly electron-withdrawing by induction.

options.label: D
options.text: The methoxy group reacts directly with the electrophile first.

questions.correct_answer: Lone pair donation from oxygen provides an additional, fourth resonance contributor for ortho and para sigma complexes where every atom has a full octet.
questions.explanation: Resonance donation from the oxygen lone pair stabilizes the arenium ion selectively at ortho and para attack positions with a full-octet structure.

questions.question: Why does a nitro group (-NO₂) direct electrophilic substitution exclusively to the meta position?

options.label: A
options.text: Meta attack is an aromatic transition state.

options.label: B
options.text: Ortho and para attack place a positive charge directly on the ring carbon bonded to the positively charged nitro nitrogen (adjacent positive charges), heavily destabilizing those pathways.

options.label: C
options.text: The nitro group donates electrons to the meta position.

options.label: D
options.text: The nitro group forms a covalent bond with the electrophile.

questions.correct_answer: Ortho and para attack place a positive charge directly on the ring carbon bonded to the positively charged nitro nitrogen (adjacent positive charges), heavily destabilizing those pathways.
questions.explanation: Ortho/para attack creates an exceptionally high-energy contributor with adjacent positive charges; meta attack avoids this electrostatic penalty.

questions.question: Why are halogen substituents deactivating toward EAS yet ortho/para directing?

options.label: A
options.text: Halogens only react at high temperatures.

options.label: B
options.text: Halogens are strong electron donors by induction.

options.label: C
options.text: Strong inductive electron withdrawal (electronegativity) deactivates the ring overall, but lone pair resonance donation selectively stabilizes ortho/para arenium ions.

options.label: D
options.text: Halogens form cyclic halonium ions with the whole ring.

questions.correct_answer: Strong inductive electron withdrawal (electronegativity) deactivates the ring overall, but lone pair resonance donation selectively stabilizes ortho/para arenium ions.
questions.explanation: Inductive withdrawal deactivates the ring (slowing rate), while lone pair resonance donation stabilizes ortho/para transition states (governing regiochemistry).

questions.question: What is the key intermediate in the nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) of 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene by methoxide?

options.label: A
options.text: A resonance-stabilized cyclohexadienyl carbanion (Meisenheimer complex) where the negative charge is delocalized onto the ortho/para nitro oxygens.

options.label: B
options.text: A benzyne intermediate with a formal triple bond.

options.label: C
options.text: An arenium cation intermediate.

options.label: D
options.text: A phenyl radical intermediate.

questions.correct_answer: A resonance-stabilized cyclohexadienyl carbanion (Meisenheimer complex) where the negative charge is delocalized onto the ortho/para nitro oxygens.
questions.explanation: Nucleophilic addition to an electron-poor aryl halide forms an anionic Meisenheimer complex stabilized by electron-withdrawing nitro groups.

questions.question: What is the structural nature of the benzyne intermediate formed when chlorobenzene reacts with KNH₂ in liquid NH₃?

options.label: A
options.text: A 7-membered cycloheptatrienyl radical.

options.label: B
options.text: A radical anion with an open ring.

options.label: C
options.text: A planar aromatic dication.

options.label: D
options.text: A reactive, strained neutral intermediate containing a formal triple bond in the ring, where the new π bond is formed by sideways overlap of two sp² orbitals in the ring plane.

questions.correct_answer: A reactive, strained neutral intermediate containing a formal triple bond in the ring, where the new π bond is formed by sideways overlap of two sp² orbitals in the ring plane.
questions.explanation: Elimination of HCl generates benzyne, featuring a highly strained in-plane π bond formed from adjacent sp² orbitals.

questions.question: What is the role of copper(I) salts in the Sandmeyer reaction of aryldiazonium salts?

options.label: A
options.text: Cu(I) transfers an electron to the diazonium ion (SET), generating an aryl radical and N₂ gas; the aryl radical is then captured by halide/cyanide from Cu(II).

options.label: B
options.text: Cu(I) acts as a Brønsted acid that protonates the diazonium group.

options.label: C
options.text: Cu(I) forms an insoluble precipitate with nitrogen.

options.label: D
options.text: Cu(I) oxidizes the aromatic ring to quinone.

questions.correct_answer: Cu(I) transfers an electron to the diazonium ion (SET), generating an aryl radical and N₂ gas; the aryl radical is then captured by halide/cyanide from Cu(II).
questions.explanation: Copper(I) catalyzes single-electron transfer, driving loss of N₂ gas and generation of a reactive aryl radical intermediate.

options.text: Attack of the aromatic π system on the electrophilic Br⁺ equivalent (Br₂·FeBr₃) to form the non-aromatic resonance-stabilized arenium ion (sigma complex).

options.label: B
options.text: Dissociation of bromobenzene into ions.

options.label: C
options.text: Coordination of FeBr₃ with benzene.

options.label: D
options.text: Deprotonation of the arenium ion by FeBr₄⁻.

questions.correct_answer: Attack of the aromatic π system on the electrophilic Br⁺ equivalent (Br₂·FeBr₃) to form the non-aromatic resonance-stabilized arenium ion (sigma complex).
questions.explanation: Formation of the sigma complex disrupts aromaticity, making it the slow, rate-determining endothermic step.

questions.question: Why is the second step (deprotonation of the arenium ion) in EAS extraordinarily fast and exergonic?

options.label: A
options.text: The arenium ion is an explosive intermediate.

options.label: B
options.text: The base FeBr₄⁻ is a superacid.

options.label: C
options.text: The reaction releases elemental bromine gas.

options.label: D
options.text: Loss of a proton from the sp³ carbon rehybridizes it to sp², instantly restoring the massive 150 kJ/mol aromatic resonance stabilization energy of the benzene ring.

questions.correct_answer: Loss of a proton from the sp³ carbon rehybridizes it to sp², instantly restoring the massive 150 kJ/mol aromatic resonance stabilization energy of the benzene ring.
questions.explanation: Regaining aromaticity provides a powerful thermodynamic driving force that makes deprotonation extremely rapid.

questions.question: How is the active electrophile (NO₂⁺) generated in the nitration of benzene by HNO₃ / H₂SO₄?

options.label: A
options.text: Sulfuric acid protonates the hydroxyl oxygen of nitric acid to form H₂O⁺-NO₂, which spontaneously loses water to generate the linear nitronium cation (O=N⁺=O).

options.label: B
options.text: Nitric acid directly attacks benzene without acid catalysis.

options.label: C
options.text: Sulfuric acid oxidizes nitrogen dioxide to nitrate.

options.label: D
options.text: Nitric acid undergoes homolytic cleavage to NO₂ radicals.

questions.correct_answer: Sulfuric acid protonates the hydroxyl oxygen of nitric acid to form H₂O⁺-NO₂, which spontaneously loses water to generate the linear nitronium cation (O=N⁺=O).
questions.explanation: Protonation of nitric acid turns -OH into water, a good leaving group, expelling H₂O to liberate the powerful nitronium electrophile.

questions.question: Why do Friedel-Crafts acylations avoid carbocation rearrangements whereas Friedel-Crafts alkylations frequently rearrange?

options.label: A
options.text: Acylation proceeds via an SN2 mechanism on the ring.

options.label: B
options.text: Acylium ions are too small to undergo rearrangements.

options.label: C
options.text: Acyl halides generate resonance-stabilized acylium ions [R-C⁺=O ↔ R-C≡O⁺] where all atoms satisfy the octet rule, preventing 1,2-hydride or alkyl shifts.

options.label: D
options.text: Aluminum chloride destroys all carbocations.

questions.correct_answer: Acyl halides generate resonance-stabilized acylium ions [R-C⁺=O ↔ R-C≡O⁺] where all atoms satisfy the octet rule, preventing 1,2-hydride or alkyl shifts.
questions.explanation: The acylium ion is resonance-stabilized with an octet-complete [R-C≡O⁺] major contributor, making it immune to skeletal rearrangements.

questions.question: Why does a methoxy group (-OCH₃) direct incoming electrophiles predominantly to the ortho and para positions?

options.label: A
options.text: The methoxy group is strongly electron-withdrawing by induction.

options.label: B
options.text: The methoxy group reacts directly with the electrophile first.

options.label: C
options.text: The methoxy group sterically blocks the meta positions.

options.label: D
options.text: Lone pair donation from oxygen provides an additional, fourth resonance contributor for ortho and para sigma complexes where every atom has a full octet.

questions.correct_answer: Lone pair donation from oxygen provides an additional, fourth resonance contributor for ortho and para sigma complexes where every atom has a full octet.
questions.explanation: Resonance donation from the oxygen lone pair stabilizes the arenium ion selectively at ortho and para attack positions with a full-octet structure.

questions.question: Why does a nitro group (-NO₂) direct electrophilic substitution exclusively to the meta position?

options.label: A
options.text: The nitro group forms a covalent bond with the electrophile.

options.label: B
options.text: Ortho and para attack place a positive charge directly on the ring carbon bonded to the positively charged nitro nitrogen (adjacent positive charges), heavily destabilizing those pathways.

options.label: C
options.text: The nitro group donates electrons to the meta position.

options.label: D
options.text: Meta attack is an aromatic transition state.

questions.correct_answer: Ortho and para attack place a positive charge directly on the ring carbon bonded to the positively charged nitro nitrogen (adjacent positive charges), heavily destabilizing those pathways.
questions.explanation: Ortho/para attack creates an exceptionally high-energy contributor with adjacent positive charges; meta attack avoids this electrostatic penalty.

questions.question: What is the structural nature of the benzyne intermediate formed when chlorobenzene reacts with KNH₂ in liquid NH₃?

options.label: A
options.text: A reactive, strained neutral intermediate containing a formal triple bond in the ring, where the new π bond is formed by sideways overlap of two sp² orbitals in the ring plane.

options.label: B
options.text: A planar aromatic dication.

options.label: C
options.text: A 7-membered cycloheptatrienyl radical.

options.label: D
options.text: A radical anion with an open ring.

questions.correct_answer: A reactive, strained neutral intermediate containing a formal triple bond in the ring, where the new π bond is formed by sideways overlap of two sp² orbitals in the ring plane.
questions.explanation: Elimination of HCl generates benzyne, featuring a highly strained in-plane π bond formed from adjacent sp² orbitals.

questions.question: What is the role of copper(I) salts in the Sandmeyer reaction of aryldiazonium salts?

options.label: A
options.text: Cu(I) acts as a Brønsted acid that protonates the diazonium group.

options.label: B
options.text: Cu(I) oxidizes the aromatic ring to quinone.

options.label: C
options.text: Cu(I) transfers an electron to the diazonium ion (SET), generating an aryl radical and N₂ gas; the aryl radical is then captured by halide/cyanide from Cu(II).

options.label: D
options.text: Cu(I) forms an insoluble precipitate with nitrogen.

questions.correct_answer: Cu(I) transfers an electron to the diazonium ion (SET), generating an aryl radical and N₂ gas; the aryl radical is then captured by halide/cyanide from Cu(II).
questions.explanation: Copper(I) catalyzes single-electron transfer, driving loss of N₂ gas and generation of a reactive aryl radical intermediate.

questions.question: Why are halogen substituents deactivating toward EAS yet ortho/para directing?

options.label: A
options.text: Halogens form cyclic halonium ions with the whole ring.

options.label: B
options.text: Strong inductive electron withdrawal (electronegativity) deactivates the ring overall, but lone pair resonance donation selectively stabilizes ortho/para arenium ions.

options.label: C
options.text: Halogens are strong electron donors by induction.

options.label: D
options.text: Halogens only react at high temperatures.

questions.correct_answer: Strong inductive electron withdrawal (electronegativity) deactivates the ring overall, but lone pair resonance donation selectively stabilizes ortho/para arenium ions.
questions.explanation: Inductive withdrawal deactivates the ring (slowing rate), while lone pair resonance donation stabilizes ortho/para transition states (governing regiochemistry).

questions.question: What is the key intermediate in the nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) of 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene by methoxide?

options.label: A
options.text: An arenium cation intermediate.

options.label: B
options.text: A phenyl radical intermediate.

options.label: C
options.text: A benzyne intermediate with a formal triple bond.

options.label: D
options.text: A resonance-stabilized cyclohexadienyl carbanion (Meisenheimer complex) where the negative charge is delocalized onto the ortho/para nitro oxygens.

questions.correct_answer: A resonance-stabilized cyclohexadienyl carbanion (Meisenheimer complex) where the negative charge is delocalized onto the ortho/para nitro oxygens.
questions.explanation: Nucleophilic addition to an electron-poor aryl halide forms an anionic Meisenheimer complex stabilized by electron-withdrawing nitro groups.
